1: # Run control
2: 
3: How to see what is running, what it is doing, and what to do when a controller
4: is gone.
5: 
6: ## Who is running
7: 
8: Every runtime attempt claims a live-run entry at the PROJECT root the moment it
9: claims its attempt (`claimRuntimeAttempt`). `uh ps` reads that registry, merges
10: in whatever each run's `runtime-control.json` currently says, and scans the
11: harness tree for pre-registry `runtime-control.json` files. The answer comes
12: back in under a second even on a large fixture, and it never needs the model.
13: 
14: ```bash
15: # One line per live run, from the project root.
16: uh ps
17: 
18: # Machine-readable: schema, counts, and the full record per run.
19: uh ps --json
20: 
21: # Include runs that already settled, kept for 24 h ("what just ran?").
22: uh ps --all
23: ```
24: 
25: Each line carries the run id, mission, team role (for team workers), runtime and
26: model, verdict, turns, denials, heartbeat age, the last tool and its age, and
27: the native pids in the controller's process tree:
28: 
29: ```
30: 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3  wave-audit-0  team=live-runs  command-code/gpt-5  live  turns=12  denials=0  hb=2s  last=edit_file (3s)  pids=3140,3141
31: ```
32: 
33: `uh status` also prints a single summary line from the same function:
34: 
35: ```
36: Live runs: 4 (orphaned: 0)
37: ```
38: 
39: ### Verdicts
40: 
41: | Verdict | Meaning | What to do |
42: |---|---|---|
43: | `live` | The controller process is alive and the run reports `running` with a fresh heartbeat. | Nothing — it is working. |
44: | `orphaned` | The run reports `running` but its controller pid is **gone**. Tokens may still be burning in a detached child. **This is the incident case.** | `uh kill --orphans` (see [Stopping runs](#stopping-runs)). `uh ps` exits `3` when any run is orphaned. |
45: | `stale` | The controller is alive but its heartbeat is older than twice the stall window (~2 min by default). | Check `last=` and the run's `events.ndjson`; the controller may be wedged. |
46: | `settled` | Terminal status (`passed`, `failed`, `blocked`, `cancelled`). Shown only with `--all`, kept for 24 h. | Nothing — it is finished. |
47: 
48: ### Exit codes
49: 
50: | Code | Meaning |
51: |---|---|
52: | `0` | Nothing is orphaned. |
53: | `3` | At least one discovered run is orphaned. |
54: | `1` | `uh ps` itself failed (bad `--root`, unreadable project). |
55: 
56: ### Where the registry lives
57: 
58: - Registry: `.harness/live-runs/<run_id>.json` under the project root
59:   (`{ schema_version: "uh.live-run.v0", run_id, mission_id, runtime, model?,
60:   team?: { mission_id, role }, artifact_root, control_path, controller_pid,
61:   started_at, status?, stop_code?, settled_at? }`).
62: - The project root is the nearest ancestor of an artifact root that holds
63:   `.harness/project.yaml`. A team worker's artifact root lives under
64:   `.harness/missions/<team>/team/artifacts/<run>/workers/<role>` and registers
65:   with its team mission id and role.
66: - The registry directory is gitignored (`.harness/live-runs/`) — it is local
67:   execution state, not a publication input.
68: 
69: ### When a run is orphaned
70: 
71: `uh ps` tells you it happened; it does not kill anything on its own. `uh kill`
72: does the stopping.
73: 
74: ```bash
75: # See the orphaned run and its native process tree.
76: uh ps
77: 
78: # Settle every orphaned run (and nothing else) from the project root.
79: uh kill --orphans
80: 
81: # Cancel an owned local run by id (writes a cancel request the controller reads).
82: uh mission cancel --mission <mission-id> --run-id <run-id> --root <project>
83: ```
84: 
85: `uh mission cancel` resolves the run through the same discovery `uh ps` uses, so
86: `--root` may be the project root even when the run is a team worker whose
87: `runtime-control.json` lives deeper in the harness tree.
88: 
89: ## Asking for a report
90: 
91: `uh ps` tells you *which* runs exist and their verdict. `uh report` answers the
92: follow-up — "what is this run doing right now?" — for one run, in under a second
93: and without spending a token. It reads only what is already on disk (the run's
94: `runtime-control.json` and its `events.ndjson`) and never starts a controller or
95: calls a model.
96: 
97: ```bash
98: # One run, by id or by a unique prefix of one.
99: uh report 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3
100: uh report 20260922T101500Z-a1b2
101: 
102: # Machine-readable, plus the projection knobs.
103: uh report 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3 --json
104: uh report 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3 --last 20   # project the last 20 tool calls (default: 10)
105: uh report 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3 --full      # read the whole events.ndjson, not just its last 256 KB
106: ```
107: 
108: A report carries:
109: 
110: - **Mission, team role, runtime and model** — the run's identity, from the live-run
111:   registry and its control file. (A registered run records its model; a
112:   pre-registry run discovered by scan may not have one.)
113: - **Liveness verdict** — the same `live` / `orphaned` / `stale` / `settled`
114:   decision `uh ps` makes, against the same process lister.
115: - **Elapsed, turns, denials** — elapsed is `started_at` to the settled time (or
116:   now); turns and the denial count come from `runtime-control.json`.
117: - **Denials, with guard class and target** — each denial in the stream, reduced to
118:   its guard class (`write_outside`, `git_mutation`, `package_install`,
119:   `network_client`, and the other `ToolGuardClass` values, or `denied` when the
120:   stream disclosed no finer class) and its **relative** target.
121: - **Tokens and cost** — reported when the stream carries them; otherwise `null`
122:   with a `tokens_unknown_reason` / `cost_unknown_reason`. Cost is never guessed:
123:   a price the runtime reported is `reported`, a harness estimate from
124:   `.harness/prices.yaml` is `estimated`, and anything else stays unknown.
125: - **Activity** — the last N completed tool calls, projected with the same
126:   `projectActivity` the loop probe uses: tool, kind, target, ok, error class and
127:   the age of the completion.
128: - **Loop signals** — `identical_repeats`, `alternating_pairs` and
129:   `distinct_targets` over that window, computed deterministically with no model.
130: - **Files written so far** — the distinct write targets that completed
131:   successfully, as relative paths.
132: - **Last assistant text** — the last assistant-authored text, bounded to 600
133:   characters and scrubbed of recognizable credentials.
134: 
135: Two guarantees hold for every field: no absolute path and no credential is ever
136: printed. Guard targets and written files are resolved relative to the run's
137: working directory (or to the bounded placeholders `<outside>` / `<pattern>` /
138: `unknown`), and the assistant text is passed through a conservative key/token
139: redactor before it is bounded.
140: 
141: By default only the **last 256 KB** of `events.ndjson` is read — the tail is
142: where the current window lives, and it keeps the answer instant even on a huge
143: log. `--full` reads the whole file when you need the history the tail dropped
144: (for example, an early usage event that prices the run).
145: 
146: Exit codes: `0` on success, `1` when the run cannot be resolved (unknown or
147: ambiguous id) or the report itself fails.
148: 
149: ## Stopping runs
150: 
151: `uh kill` stops runs and proves they are dead. Targets are always resolved
152: through `discoverRuns` — the live-run registry plus the bounded harness scan —
153: so the artifact root is never something the operator has to know.
154: 
155: ```bash
156: # One run, by id or by a unique prefix of one.
157: uh kill 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3
158: uh kill 20260922T101500Z-a1b2
159: 
160: # Everything belonging to a mission, one worker role, or a whole team.
161: uh kill --mission wave-audit-0
162: uh kill --role backend
163: uh kill --team wave-audit-0
164: 
165: # The project sweeps.
166: uh kill --all
167: uh kill --orphans
168: ```
169: 
170: For each target, in order:
171: 
172: 1. Resolve the artifact root that owns the run. A team worker's
173:    `runtime-control.json` sits under
174:    `.harness/missions/<team>/team/artifacts/<parent-run>/workers/<role>`, and
175:    that is the root the cancellation is written to.
176: 2. Ask the controller to stop with the normal `uh mission cancel` request.
177: 3. Wait up to `--wait-ms` (default `10000`) for the controller and every native
178:    process in its tree to exit, against the same process lister `uh ps` uses.
179: 4. If anything survives, terminate the tree: `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`
180:    through PowerShell on Windows, a SIGKILL of the process group on POSIX.
181:    `--force` skips steps 2 and 3 and goes straight here.
182: 5. Re-list the processes, settle the live-run registry entry, and report.
183: 
184: ```bash
185: # Machine-readable, and what the operator sees:
186: uh kill --team wave-audit-0 --json
187: ```
188: 
189: ```
190: 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3  wave-audit-0  team=live-runs  oh-my-pi  cancelled_gracefully  stop=cancelled  pids=3140,3141
191: 20260922T101502Z-d4e5f6  wave-audit-0  team=-          ultimate-harness-team  force_killed  stop=cancelled  pids=3100
192: team=wave-audit-0  run=20260922T101500Z-parent  team-state cancelled
193: matched=3 gracefully=2 forced=1 orphans=0 alive=0 errors=0
194: ```
195: 
196: ### Outcomes
197: 
198: | Outcome | Meaning |
199: |---|---|
200: | `cancelled_gracefully` | The controller settled its own run and its process tree is gone. |
201: | `force_killed` | The controller never settled or never exited; the owned tree was terminated and the re-list confirms it is gone. |
202: | `still_alive` | Pids survived even the forced kill. They are listed as `surviving=` and the command exits `1`. |
203: | `orphan_settled` | The controller pid was already gone, so no process was touched; the record was closed with `stop_code: controller_lost`. |
204: | `skipped_settled` | The run had already settled for another reason; nothing was asked of it. |
205: | `error` | That target could not be stopped (unreadable artifacts, a settlement conflict). Other targets are still processed. |
206: 
207: Exit codes: `0` when every matched target is stopped, `1` when anything is
208: `still_alive` or `error`, or when the command itself failed (bad selector,
209: ambiguous prefix, unknown run id).
210: 
211: ### Orphans
212: 
213: An orphaned run has no controller to ask and no tree to chase, so `uh kill
214: <run-id>` never terminates anything for it: it closes the record through the
215: same reconcile path the native guardian feeds, writing a `controller_lost`
216: receipt first when the guardian never got the chance (the POSIX and
217: pre-guardian cases), then reconciling canonical artifacts. `uh kill --orphans`
218: does every orphaned run at once — the same set that makes `uh ps` exit `3`.
219: 
220: That receipt attests that the owned tree is gone, so it is withheld when the
221: process table still parents live processes to the dead controller pid (Windows
222: keeps a stale `ParentProcessId`, so a detached runtime stays attributable
223: there). Such a run is reported `still_alive` with those pids and exits `1`; the
224: record is only closed by `--force`, which says "I know a native process is
225: still parented there, close the record anyway" and still does not signal it.
226: 
227: ### Team cascade
228: 
229: `--team <id>` stops a team in the only safe order: each worker run first, then
230: the team controller that hosted them, then `team-state.json` is marked
231: cancelled so the leader's integration never lands. Because a team controller is
232: shared by its workers, `uh kill <worker-run-id>` on its own only waits for that
233: worker's own settlement — it will not kill a pid its siblings are still running
234: under. Use `--team` (or `--all`) for that.
235: 
236: ### What it will not do
237: 
238: * A pid is signalled only when it is a run's recorded controller pid or a
239:   descendant of it, taken from the process snapshot captured before anything
240:   was asked to stop. No other process on the machine is reachable from here.
241: * An empty process table is a hard error, not a licence to declare every run
242:   dead.
243: * Nothing is inferred from a stale heartbeat alone; liveness is the process
244:   lister's answer.
245: 
246: ## Steering a worker
247: 
248: A worker can be nudged mid-run only by stopping it and resuming its native
249: session with a message. `uh steer` validates the request, then has the run's
250: owning controller perform the steer:
251: 
252: ```bash
253: # Message the run: its controller stops the attempt (stop code `steered`) and
254: # resumes the same native session with the message as the first instruction.
255: uh steer 20260922T101500Z-a1b2c3 "Skip the retry loop; the endpoint already returns 429."
256: 
257: # Ask for a status report before the worker continues.
258: uh steer <run-id> "Continue" --report
259: 
260: # Machine-readable outcome.
261: uh steer <run-id> "<message>" --json
262: ```
263: 
264: `--report` prepends a fixed request: write a report in the shape "done so far /
265: in progress / blocked on / next three actions / files touched" before anything
266: else, then continue.
267: 
268: ### Preflight — everything is validated before the run is touched
269: 
270: `uh steer` refuses, and changes nothing, unless all of the following hold:
271: 
272: 1. The run exists (by id or a unique prefix), resolved exactly like `uh ps`
273:    does — from the project root, including team workers under their own
274:    artifact roots.
275: 2. A native session id is recorded for the attempt.
276: 3. The adapter manifest resolves from the **project root** that owns
277:    `.harness/adapters` (the nearest ancestor of the run's artifact scope). A
278:    team worker's scope lives under
279:    `.harness/missions/<team>/team/artifacts/...` and holds no adapters of its
280:    own, so the manifest is never looked up there.
281: 4. The runtime has a native resume path (Command Code, oh-my-pi, Claude Code).
282: 
283: A refusal is a clear message and no side effect: no stop is signalled and no
284: steer request is written.
285: 
286: ### The owning controller resumes it
287: 
288: When a live controller owns the attempt (`uh ps` says `live`), steer writes a
289: `steer-request.json` (message, `report` flag, `requested_at`) next to the run's
290: `runtime-control.json` and signals the attempt to stop. The controller's
291: recovery loop (`runWithRuntimeRecovery`) then:
292: 
293: - consumes the request (it is deleted, so it can never be replayed),
294: - records the stopped attempt as `stop_code: steered` — a resumable, non-terminal
295:   stop, never a bare `cancelled`,
296: - starts the next attempt with `resume_from_run = <run-id>` and the operator's
297:   message as the first instruction, and
298: - records the steer in the attempt lineage (`runtime-recovery.json` on the new
299:   run carries `source_stop_code: steered` and the message as its notes).
300: 
301: A steered attempt does **not** count against the mission's
302: `recovery.max_resumes` budget — an operator message is authorized outside the
303: automatic loop. Because the resume happens inside the controller, a team
304: worker keeps running inside its team controller and is integrated normally
305: instead of being treated as a finished worker.
306: 
307: ### When no live controller owns the run
308: 
309: If the controller is gone (`uh ps` reports `orphaned`), steer falls back to the
310: older path — but only after the same preflight succeeded. It asks the settled
311: run's remaining owner to stop, then starts a new run for the same mission, in
312: the same artifact root and sandbox, bound to `resume_from_run = <run-id>`, and
313: records the operator lineage both ways: `resumed_from` on the new run and
314: `resumed_by` on the old one, with `resume_origin: "operator"` in
315: `runs/<run-id>/resume-link.json` on each.
316: 
317: **The honest caveat**: steering is not a live channel. It costs a stop and a
318: restart of the native session. The transcript and prior work survive because the
319: runtime resumes the same session, but the worker re-reads its context before it
320: acts on the message.
321: 
322: ## Resuming
323: 
324: `uh resume` continues a run that has already settled, without a new message:
325: 
326: ```bash
327: uh resume <run-id> [--notes "<text>"] [--json]
328: ```
329: 
330: It refuses a run that is still live — steer that one instead — and refuses a
331: runtime with no session resume path:
332: 
333: ```
334: unsupported: <runtime> has no session resume
335: ```
336: 
337: For a supported runtime (Command Code, oh-my-pi, Claude Code) it starts a new
338: run in the same mission, artifact root, and sandbox with
339: `resume_from_run = <run-id>`, and records the lineage both ways: `resumed_from`
340: on the new run and `resumed_by` on the old one, with `resume_origin: "operator"`
341: in `runs/<run-id>/resume-link.json` on each. Operator resumes are authorized
342: outside the automatic recovery loop, so they never spend the mission's
343: `recovery.max_resumes` budget.
344: 
345: ## Related
346: 
347: - `uh status` / `uh status --json` include live-run counts.
348: - `uh mission cancel` — cancel an owned local run.
349: - `uh kill` — stop runs by id, role, mission, team, `--all` or `--orphans`.
350: - `uh steer` — message a run; its controller stops the attempt (`steered`) and resumes the session.
351: - `uh resume` — continue a settled run's session as a new run.
352: - Team fan-out and worker artifact layout: `docs/runbooks/resource-wave-smoke.md`.
